sanskrit_shloka:
तदात्मानात्मनोः सम्यग्विवेकेनैव सिध्यति ।
ततो विवेकः कर्तव्यः प्रत्यगात्मसदात्मनोः ॥ २0३ ॥
transliteration:
tadātmānātmanoḥ samyagvivekenaiva sidhyati |
tato vivekaḥ kartavyaḥ pratyagātmasadātmanoḥ || 203 ||
translation: This realisation is attained by a perfect discrimination between the Self and the non-Self. Therefore one must strive for the discrimination between the individual soul and the eternal Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This realisation is attained by a perfect discrimination between the Self and the non-Self. Therefore one must strive for the discrimination between the individual soul and the eternal Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
जलं पङ्कवदत्यन्तं पङ्कापाये जलं स्फुटम् ।
यथा भाति तथात्मापि दोषाभावे स्फुटप्रभः ॥ २0४ ॥
transliteration:
jalaṃ paṅkavadatyantaṃ paṅkāpāye jalaṃ sphuṭam |
yathā bhāti tathātmāpi doṣābhāve sphuṭaprabhaḥ || 204 ||
translation: Just as the water which is very muddy again appears as transparent water when the mud is removed, so the Ātman also manifests Its undimmed lustre when the taint has been removed.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the water which is very muddy again appears as transparent water when the mud is removed, so the Ātman also manifests Its undimmed lustre when the taint has been removed.

sanskrit_shloka:
असन्निवृत्तौ तु सदात्मना स्फुटं प्रतीतिरेतस्य भवेत्प्रतीचः ।
ततो निरासः करणीय एव सदात्मनः साध्वहमादिवस्तुनः ॥ २0५ ॥
transliteration:
asannivṛttau tu sadātmanā sphuṭaṃ pratītiretasya bhavetpratīcaḥ |
tato nirāsaḥ karaṇīya eva sadātmanaḥ sādhvahamādivastunaḥ || 205 ||
translation: When the unreal ceases to exist, this very individual soul is definitely realised as the eternal Self. Therefore one must make it a point completely to remove things like egoism from the eternal Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the unreal ceases to exist, this very individual soul is definitely realised as the eternal Self. Therefore one must make it a point completely to remove things like egoism from the eternal Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतो नायं परात्मा स्याद्विज्ञानमायाशब्दभाक् ।
विकारित्वाज्जडत्वाच्च परिच्छिन्नत्वहेतुतः ।
दृश्यत्वाद्व्यभिचारित्वान्नानित्यो नित्य इष्यते ॥ २0६ ॥
transliteration:
ato nāyaṃ parātmā syādvijñānaMāyāśabdabhāk |
vikāritvājjaḍatvācca paricchinnatvahetutaḥ |
dṛśyatvādvyabhicāritvānnānityo nitya iṣyate || 206 ||
translation: This knowledge sheath (Vijñānamāyā Kośa) that we have been speaking of, cannot be the Supreme Self for the following reasons - because it is subject to change, is insentient, is a limited thing, an object of the senses, and is not constantly present: An unreal thing cannot indeed be taken for the real Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This knowledge sheath (Vijñānamāyā Kośa) that we have been speaking of, cannot be the Supreme Self for the following reasons - because it is subject to change, is insentient, is a limited thing, an object of the senses, and is not constantly present: An unreal thing cannot indeed be taken for the real Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
असन्निवृत्तौ तु सदात्मना स्फुटं प्रतीतिरेतस्य भवेत्प्रतीचः ।
ततो निरासः करणीय एव सदात्मनः साध्वहमादिवस्तुनः ॥ २0५ ॥
transliteration:
asannivṛttau tu sadātmanā sphuṭaṃ pratītiretasya bhavetpratīcaḥ |
tato nirāsaḥ karaṇīya eva sadātmanaḥ sādhvahamādivastunaḥ || 205 ||
translation: When the unreal ceases to exist, this very individual soul is definitely realised as the eternal Self. Therefore one must make it a point completely to remove things like egoism from the eternal Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the unreal ceases to exist, this very individual soul is definitely realised as the eternal Self. Therefore one must make it a point completely to remove things like egoism from the eternal Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतो नायं परात्मा स्याद्विज्ञानमायाशब्दभाक् ।
विकारित्वाज्जडत्वाच्च परिच्छिन्नत्वहेतुतः ।
दृश्यत्वाद्व्यभिचारित्वान्नानित्यो नित्य इष्यते ॥ २0६ ॥
transliteration:
ato nāyaṃ parātmā syādvijñānaMāyāśabdabhāk |
vikāritvājjaḍatvācca paricchinnatvahetutaḥ |
dṛśyatvādvyabhicāritvānnānityo nitya iṣyate || 206 ||
translation: This knowledge sheath (Vijñānamāyā Kośa) that we have been speaking of, cannot be the Supreme Self for the following reasons - because it is subject to change, is insentient, is a limited thing, an object of the senses, and is not constantly present: An unreal thing cannot indeed be taken for the real Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This knowledge sheath (Vijñānamāyā Kośa) that we have been speaking of, cannot be the Supreme Self for the following reasons - because it is subject to change, is insentient, is a limited thing, an object of the senses, and is not constantly present: An unreal thing cannot indeed be taken for the real Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
आनन्दप्रतिबिम्बचुम्बिततनुर्वृत्तिस्तमोजृम्भिता स्यादानन्दमायाः प्रियादिगुणकः स्वेष्टार्थलाभोदयः ।
पुण्यस्यानुभवे विभाति कृतिनामानन्दरूपः स्वयं सर्वो नन्दति यत्र साधु तनुभृन्मात्रः प्रयत्नं विना ॥ २0७ ॥
transliteration:
ānandapratibimbacumbitatanurvṛttistamojṛmbhitā syādānandaMāyāḥ priyādiguṇakaḥ sveṣṭārthalābhodayaḥ |
puṇyasyānubhave vibhāti kṛtināmānandarūpaḥ svayaṃ sarvo nandati yatra sādhu tanubhṛnmātraḥ prayatnaṃ vinā || 207 ||
translation: The blissful sheath (Ānandamāyā Kośa) is that modification of Nescience which manifests itself catching a reflection of the Ātman which is Bliss Absolute; whose attributes are pleasure and the rest; and which appears in view when some object agreeable to oneself presents itself. It makes itself spontaneously felt by the fortunate during the fruition of their virtuous deeds; from which every corporeal being derives great joy without the least effort.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The blissful sheath (Ānandamāyā Kośa) is that modification of Nescience which manifests itself catching a reflection of the Ātman which is Bliss Absolute; whose attributes are pleasure and the rest; and which appears in view when some object agreeable to oneself presents itself. It makes itself spontaneously felt by the fortunate during the fruition of their virtuous deeds; from which every corporeal being derives great joy without the least effort.

sanskrit_shloka:
आनन्दमायाकोशस्य सुषुप्तौ स्फूर्तिरुत्कटा ।
स्वप्नजागरयोरीषदिष्टसंदर्शनाविना ॥ २0८ ॥
transliteration:
ānandaMāyākośasya suṣuptau sphūrtirutkaṭā |
svapnajāgarayorīṣadiṣṭasaṃdarśanāvinā || 208 ||
translation: The blissful sheath has its fullest play during profound sleep, while in the dreaming and wakeful states it has only a partial manifestation, occasioned by the sight of agreeable objects and so forth.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The blissful sheath has its fullest play during profound sleep, while in the dreaming and wakeful states it has only a partial manifestation, occasioned by the sight of agreeable objects and so forth.

sanskrit_shloka:
नैवायमानन्दमायाः परात्मा सोपाधिकत्वात्प्रकृतेर्विकारात् ।
कार्यत्वहेतोः सुकृतक्रियाया विकारसङ्घातसमाहितत्वात् ॥ २0९ ॥
transliteration:
naivāyamānandaMāyāḥ parātmā sopādhikatvātprakṛtervikārāt |
kāryatvahetoḥ sukṛtakriyāyā vikārasaṅghātasamāhitatvāt || 209 ||
translation: Nor is the blissful sheath the Supreme Self, because it is endowed with the changeful attributes, is a modification of the Prakriti, is the effect of past good deeds, and imbedded in the other sheaths which are modifications.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Nor is the blissful sheath the Supreme Self, because it is endowed with the changeful attributes, is a modification of the Prakriti, is the effect of past good deeds, and imbedded in the other sheaths which are modifications.

sanskrit_shloka:
पञ्चानामपि कोशानां निषेधे युक्तितः श्रुतेः ।
तन्निषेधावधि साक्षी बोधरूपोऽवशिष्यते ॥ २१0 ॥
transliteration:
pañcānāmapi kośānāṃ niṣedhe yuktitaḥ śruteḥ |
tanniṣedhāvadhi sākṣī bodharūpo'vaśiṣyate || 210 ||
translation: When all the five sheaths have been eliminated by the reasoning on Shruti passages, what remains as the culminating point of the process, is the Witness, the Knowledge Absolute – the Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When all the five sheaths have been eliminated by the reasoning on Shruti passages, what remains as the culminating point of the process, is the Witness, the Knowledge Absolute – the Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
योऽयमात्मा स्वयंज्योतिः पञ्चकोशविलक्षणः ।
अवस्थात्रयसाक्षी सन्निर्विकारो निरञ्जनः सदानन्दः स विज्ञेयः स्वात्मत्वेन विपश्चिता ॥ २११ ॥
transliteration:
yo'yamātmā svayaṃjyotiḥ pañcakośavilakṣaṇaḥ |
avasthātrayasākṣī sannirvikāro nirañjanaḥ sadānandaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ svātmatvena vipaścitā || 211 ||
translation: This self-effulgent Ātman which is distinct from the five sheaths, the Witness of the three states, the Real, the Changeless, the Untainted, the everlasting Bliss – is to be realised by the wise man as his own Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This self-effulgent Ātman which is distinct from the five sheaths, the Witness of the three states, the Real, the Changeless, the Untainted, the everlasting Bliss – is to be realised by the wise man as his own Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
शिष्य उवाच मिथ्यात्वेन निषिद्धेषु कोशेष्वेतेषु पञ्चसु ।
सर्वाभावं विना किंचिन्न पश्याम्यत्र हे गुरो विज्ञेयं किमु वस्त्वस्ति स्वात्मनात्मविपश्चिता ॥ २१२ ॥
transliteration:
śiṣya uvāca mithyātvena niṣiddheṣu kośeṣveteṣu pañcasu |
sarvābhāvaṃ vinā kiṃcinna paśyāmyatra he guro vijñeyaṃ kimu vastvasti svātmanātmavipaścitā || 212 ||
translation: The disciple questioned: After these five sheaths have been eliminated as unreal, I find nothing, O Master, in this universe but a Void, the absence of everything. What entity is there left forsooth with which the wise knower of the Self should realise his identity.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The disciple questioned: After these five sheaths have been eliminated as unreal, I find nothing, O Master, in this universe but a Void, the absence of everything. What entity is there left forsooth with which the wise knower of the Self should realise his identity.

sanskrit_shloka:
श्रीगुरुरुवाच सत्यमुक्तं त्वया विदन्निपुणोऽसि विचारणे ।
अहमादिविकारास्ते तदभावोऽयमप्यनु ॥ २१३ ॥
transliteration:
सर्वे येनानुभूयन्ते यः स्वयं नानुभूयते ।
तमात्मानं वेदितारं विद्दि बुद्ध्या सुसूक्ष्मया ॥ २१४
translation: 213-214. The Guru answered: Thou has rightly said, O learned man ! Thou art clever indeed in discrimination. That by which all those modifications such as egoism as well as their subsequent absence (during deep sleep) are perceived, but which Itself is not perceived, know thou that Ātman – the Knower – through the sharpest intellect.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: 213-214. The Guru answered: Thou has rightly said, O learned man ! Thou art clever indeed in discrimination. That by which all those modifications such as egoism as well as their subsequent absence (during deep sleep) are perceived, but which Itself is not perceived, know thou that Ātman – the Knower – through the sharpest intellect.

sanskrit_shloka:
तत्साक्षिकं भवेत्तत्तद्यद्यद्येनानुभूयते ।
कस्याप्यननुभूतार्थे साक्षित्वं नोपयुज्यते ॥ २१५ ॥
transliteration:
tatsākṣikaṃ bhavettattadyadyadyenānubhūyate |
kasyāpyananubhūtārthe sākṣitvaṃ nopayujyate || 215 ||
translation: That which is perceived by something else has for its witness the latter. When there is no agent to perceive a thing, we cannot speak of it as having been perceived at all.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is perceived by something else has for its witness the latter. When there is no agent to perceive a thing, we cannot speak of it as having been perceived at all.

sanskrit_shloka:
असौ स्वसाक्षिको भावो यतः स्वेनानुभूयते ।
अतः परं स्वयं साक्षात्प्रत्यगात्मा न चेतरः ॥ २१६ ॥
transliteration:
asau svasākṣiko bhāvo yataḥ svenānubhūyate |
ataḥ paraṃ svayaṃ sākṣātpratyagātmā na cetaraḥ || 216 ||
translation: This Ātman is a self-cognised entity because It is cognised by Itself. Hence the individual soul is itself and directly the Supreme Brahman, and nothing else.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This Ātman is a self-cognised entity because It is cognised by Itself. Hence the individual soul is itself and directly the Supreme Brahman, and nothing else.

sanskrit_shloka:
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु स्फुटतरं योऽसौ समुज्जृम्भते प्रत्यग्रूपतया सदाहमहमित्यन्तः स्फुरन्नैकधा ।
नानाकारविकारभागिन इमान् पश्यन्नहंधीमुखान् नित्यानन्दचिदात्मना स्फुरति तं विद्धि स्वमेतं हृदि ॥ २१७ ॥
transliteration:
jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu sphuṭataraṃ yo'sau samujjṛmbhate pratyagrūpatayā sadāhamahamityantaḥ sphurannaikadhā |
nānākāravikārabhāgina imān paśyannahaṃdhīmukhān nityānandacidātmanā sphurati taṃ viddhi svametaṃ hṛdi || 217 ||
translation: That which clearly manifests Itself in the states of wakefulness, dream and profound sleep; which is inwardly perceived in the mind in various forms as an unbroken series of egoistic impressions; which witnesses the egoism, the Buddhi, etc., which are of diverse forms and modifications; and which makes Itself felt as the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute; know thou this Ātman, thy own Self, within thy heart.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which clearly manifests Itself in the states of wakefulness, dream and profound sleep; which is inwardly perceived in the mind in various forms as an unbroken series of egoistic impressions; which witnesses the egoism, the Buddhi, etc., which are of diverse forms and modifications; and which makes Itself felt as the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute; know thou this Ātman, thy own Self, within thy heart.

sanskrit_shloka:
घटोदके बिम्बितमर्कबिम्बम् आलोक्य मूढो रविमेव मन्यते ।
तथा चिदाभासमुपाधिसंस्थं भ्रान्त्याहमित्येव जडोऽभिमन्यते ॥ २१८ ॥
transliteration:
ghaṭodake bimbitamarkabimbam ālokya mūḍho ravimeva manyate |
tathā cidābhāsamupādhisaṃsthaṃ bhrāntyāhamityeva jaḍo'bhimanyate || 218 ||
translation: Seeing the reflection of the sun mirrored in the water of a jar, the fool thinks it is the sun itself. Similarly the stupid man, through delusion, identifies himself with the reflection of the Chit caught in the Buddhi, which is Its superimposition.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Seeing the reflection of the sun mirrored in the water of a jar, the fool thinks it is the sun itself. Similarly the stupid man, through delusion, identifies himself with the reflection of the Chit caught in the Buddhi, which is Its superimposition.

sanskrit_shloka:
घटं जलं तद्गतमर्कबिम्बं विहाय सर्वं विनिरीक्ष्यतेऽर्कः ।
तटस्थ एतत्त्रितयावभासकः स्वयंप्रकाशो विदुषा यथा तथा ॥ २१९ ॥
transliteration:
ghaṭaṃ jalaṃ tadgatamarkabimbaṃ vihāya sarvaṃ vinirīkṣyate'rkaḥ |
taṭastha etattritayāvabhāsakaḥ svayaṃprakāśo viduṣā yathā tathā || 219 ||
translation: Just as the wise man leaves aside the jar, the water and the reflection of the sun in it, and sees the self-luminous sun which illumines these three and is independent of them;

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the wise man leaves aside the jar, the water and the reflection of the sun in it, and sees the self-luminous sun which illumines these three and is independent of them;

sanskrit_shloka:
देहं धियं चित्प्रतिबिम्बमेवं विसृज्य बुद्धौ निहितं गुहायाम् ।
द्रष्टारमात्मानमखण्डबोधं सर्वप्रकाशं सदसद्विलक्षणम् ॥ २२0 ॥
transliteration:
नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं अन्तर्बहिःशून्यमनन्यमात्मनः ।
विज्ञाय सम्यङ्निजरूपमेतत् पुमान् विपाप्मा विरजो विमृत्युः ॥ २२१ ॥
translation: 220-222. Similarly, discarding the body, the Buddhi and the reflection of the Chit in it, and realising the Witness, the Self, the Knowledge Absolute, the cause of the manifestation of everything, which is hidden in the recesses of the Buddhi, is distinct from the gross and subtle, eternal, omnipresent, all-pervading and extremely subtle, and which has neither interior nor exterior and is identical with one self – fully realising this true nature of oneself, one becomes free from sin, taint, death and grief, and becomes the embodiment of Bliss. Illumined himself, he is afraid of none. For a seeker after Liberation there is no other way to the breaking of the bonds of transmigration than the realisation of the truth of one’s own Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: 220-222. Similarly, discarding the body, the Buddhi and the reflection of the Chit in it, and realising the Witness, the Self, the Knowledge Absolute, the cause of the manifestation of everything, which is hidden in the recesses of the Buddhi, is distinct from the gross and subtle, eternal, omnipresent, all-pervading and extremely subtle, and which has neither interior nor exterior and is identical with one self – fully realising this true nature of oneself, one becomes free from sin, taint, death and grief, and becomes the embodiment of Bliss. Illumined himself, he is afraid of none. For a seeker after Liberation there is no other way to the breaking of the bonds of transmigration than the realisation of the truth of one’s own Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्माभिन्नत्वविज्ञानं भवमोक्षस्य कारणम् ।
येनाद्वितीयमानन्दं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते बुधैः ॥ २२३ ॥
transliteration:
brahmābhinnatvavijñānaṃ bhavamokṣasya kāraṇam |
yenādvitīyamānandaṃ brahma sampadyate budhaiḥ || 223 ||
translation: The realisation of one’s identity with Brahman is the cause of Liberation from the bonds of Samsara, by means of which the wise man attains Brahman, the One without a second, the Bliss Absolute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The realisation of one’s identity with Brahman is the cause of Liberation from the bonds of Samsara, by means of which the wise man attains Brahman, the One without a second, the Bliss Absolute.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मभूतस्तु संसृत्यै विद्वान्नावर्तते पुनः ।
विज्ञातव्यमतः सम्यग्ब्रह्माभिन्नत्वमात्मनः ॥ २२४ ॥
transliteration:
brahmabhūtastu saṃsṛtyai vidvānnāvartate punaḥ |
vijñātavyamataḥ samyagbrahmābhinnatvamātmanaḥ || 224 ||
translation: Once having realised Brahman, one no longer returns to the realm of transmigration. Therefore one must fully realise one’s identity with Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Once having realised Brahman, one no longer returns to the realm of transmigration. Therefore one must fully realise one’s identity with Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं ब्रह्म विशुद्धं परं स्वतःसिद्धम् ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसं प्रत्यगभिन्नं निरन्तरं जयति ॥ २२५ ॥
transliteration:
satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma viśuddhaṃ paraṃ svataḥsiddham |
nityānandaikarasaṃ pratyagabhinnaṃ nirantaraṃ jayati || 225 ||
translation: Brahman is Existence, Knowledge, Infinity, pure, supreme, self-existent, eternal and indivisible Bliss, not different (in reality) from the individual soul, and devoid of interior or exterior. It is (ever) triumphant.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Brahman is Existence, Knowledge, Infinity, pure, supreme, self-existent, eternal and indivisible Bliss, not different (in reality) from the individual soul, and devoid of interior or exterior. It is (ever) triumphant.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्माभिन्नत्वविज्ञानं भवमोक्षस्य कारणम् ।
येनाद्वितीयमानन्दं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते बुधैः ॥ २२३ ॥
transliteration:
brahmābhinnatvavijñānaṃ bhavamokṣasya kāraṇam |
yenādvitīyamānandaṃ brahma sampadyate budhaiḥ || 223 ||
translation: The realisation of one’s identity with Brahman is the cause of Liberation from the bonds of Samsara, by means of which the wise man attains Brahman, the One without a second, the Bliss Absolute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The realisation of one’s identity with Brahman is the cause of Liberation from the bonds of Samsara, by means of which the wise man attains Brahman, the One without a second, the Bliss Absolute.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मभूतस्तु संसृत्यै विद्वान्नावर्तते पुनः ।
विज्ञातव्यमतः सम्यग्ब्रह्माभिन्नत्वमात्मनः ॥ २२४ ॥
transliteration:
brahmabhūtastu saṃsṛtyai vidvānnāvartate punaḥ |
vijñātavyamataḥ samyagbrahmābhinnatvamātmanaḥ || 224 ||
translation: Once having realised Brahman, one no longer returns to the realm of transmigration. Therefore one must fully realise one’s identity with Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Once having realised Brahman, one no longer returns to the realm of transmigration. Therefore one must fully realise one’s identity with Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं ब्रह्म विशुद्धं परं स्वतःसिद्धम् ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसं प्रत्यगभिन्नं निरन्तरं जयति ॥ २२५ ॥
transliteration:
satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma viśuddhaṃ paraṃ svataḥsiddham |
nityānandaikarasaṃ pratyagabhinnaṃ nirantaraṃ jayati || 225 ||
translation: Brahman is Existence, Knowledge, Infinity, pure, supreme, self-existent, eternal and indivisible Bliss, not different (in reality) from the individual soul, and devoid of interior or exterior. It is (ever) triumphant.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Brahman is Existence, Knowledge, Infinity, pure, supreme, self-existent, eternal and indivisible Bliss, not different (in reality) from the individual soul, and devoid of interior or exterior. It is (ever) triumphant.

sanskrit_shloka:
सदिदं परमाद्वैतं स्वस्मादन्यस्य वस्तुनोऽभावात् ।
न ह्यन्यदस्ति किंचित्सम्यक्परमार्थतत्त्वबोधदशायाम् ॥ २२६ ॥
transliteration:
sadidaṃ paramādvaitaṃ svasmādanyasya vastuno'bhāvāt |
na hyanyadasti kiṃcitsamyakparamārthatattvabodhadaśāyām || 226 ||
translation: It is this Supreme Oneness which alone is real, since there is nothing else but the Self. Verily, there remains no other independent entity in the state of realisation of the highest Truth.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It is this Supreme Oneness which alone is real, since there is nothing else but the Self. Verily, there remains no other independent entity in the state of realisation of the highest Truth.

sanskrit_shloka:
यदिदं सकलं विश्वं नानारूपं प्रतीतमज्ञानात् ।
तत्सर्वं ब्रह्मैव प्रत्यस्ताशेषभावनादोषम् ॥ २२७ ॥
transliteration:
yadidaṃ sakalaṃ viśvaṃ nānārūpaṃ pratītamajñānāt |
tatsarvaṃ brahmaiva pratyastāśeṣabhāvanādoṣam || 227 ||
translation: All this universe which through ignorance appears as of diverse forms, is nothing else but Brahman which is absolutely free from all the limitations of human thought.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: All this universe which through ignorance appears as of diverse forms, is nothing else but Brahman which is absolutely free from all the limitations of human thought.

sanskrit_shloka:
मृत्कार्यभूतोऽपि मृदो न भिन्नः कुम्भोऽस्ति सर्वत्र तु मृत्स्वरूपात् ।
न कुम्भरूपं पृथगस्ति कुम्भः कुतो मृषा कल्पितनाममात्रः ॥ २२८ ॥
transliteration:
mṛtkāryabhūto'pi mṛdo na bhinnaḥ kumbho'sti sarvatra tu mṛtsvarūpāt |
na kumbharūpaṃ pṛthagasti kumbhaḥ kuto mṛṣā kalpitanāmamātraḥ || 228 ||
translation: A jar, though a modification of clay, is not different from it; everywhere the jar is essentially the same as the clay. Why then call it a jar ? It is fictitious, a fancied name merely.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: A jar, though a modification of clay, is not different from it; everywhere the jar is essentially the same as the clay. Why then call it a jar ? It is fictitious, a fancied name merely.

sanskrit_shloka:
केनापि मृद्भिन्नतया स्वरूपं घटस्य संदर्शयितुं न शक्यते ।
अतो घटः कल्पित एव मोहान् मृदेव सत्यं परमार्थभूतम् ॥ २२९ ॥
transliteration:
kenāpi mṛdbhinnatayā svarūpaṃ ghaṭasya saṃdarśayituṃ na śakyate |
ato ghaṭaḥ kalpita eva mohān mṛdeva satyaṃ paramārthabhūtam || 229 ||
translation: None can demonstrate that the essence of a jar is something other than the clay (of which it is made). Hence the jar is merely imagined (as separate) through delusion, and the component clay alone is the abiding reality in respect of it.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: None can demonstrate that the essence of a jar is something other than the clay (of which it is made). Hence the jar is merely imagined (as separate) through delusion, and the component clay alone is the abiding reality in respect of it.

sanskrit_shloka:
सद्ब्रह्मकार्यं सकलं सदेवं तन्मात्रमेतन्न ततोऽन्यदस्ति ।
अस्तीति यो वक्ति न तस्य मोहो विनिर्गतो निद्रितवत्प्रजल्पः ॥ २३0 ॥
transliteration:
sadbrahmakāryaṃ sakalaṃ sadevaṃ tanmātrametanna tato'nyadasti |
astīti yo vakti na tasya moho vinirgato nidritavatprajalpaḥ || 230 ||
translation: Similarly, the whole universe, being the effect of the real Brahman, is in reality nothing but Brahman. Its essence is That, and it does not exist apart from It. He who says it does is still under delusion – he babbles like one asleep.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Similarly, the whole universe, being the effect of the real Brahman, is in reality nothing but Brahman. Its essence is That, and it does not exist apart from It. He who says it does is still under delusion – he babbles like one asleep.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मैवेदं विश्वमित्येव वाणी श्रौती ब्रूतेऽथर्वनिष्ठा वरिष्ठा ।
तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्ममात्रं हि विश्वं नाधिष्ठानाद्भिन्नतारोपितस्य ॥ २३१ ॥
transliteration:
brahmaivedaṃ viśvamityeva vāṇī śrautī brūte'tharvaniṣṭhā variṣṭhā |
tasmādetadbrahmamātraṃ hi viśvaṃ nādhiṣṭhānādbhinnatāropitasya || 231 ||
translation: This universe is verily Brahman – such is the august pronouncement of the Atharva Veda. Therefore this universe is nothing but Brahman, for that which is superimposed (on something) has no separate existence from its substratum.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This universe is verily Brahman – such is the august pronouncement of the Atharva Veda. Therefore this universe is nothing but Brahman, for that which is superimposed (on something) has no separate existence from its substratum.

sanskrit_shloka:
सत्यं यदि स्याज्जगदेतदात्मनो ऽनन्तत्त्वहानिर्निगमाप्रमाणता ।
असत्यवादित्वमपीशितुः स्यान् नैतत्त्रयं साधु हितं महात्मनाम् ॥ २३२ ॥
transliteration:
satyaṃ yadi syājjagadetadātmano 'nantattvahānirnigamāpramāṇatā |
asatyavāditvamapīśituḥ syān naitattrayaṃ sādhu hitaṃ mahātmanām || 232 ||
translation: If the universe, as it is, be real, there would be no cessation of the dualistic element, the scriptures would be falsified, and the Lord Himself would be guilty of an untruth. None of these three is considered either desirable or wholesome by the noble- minded.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: If the universe, as it is, be real, there would be no cessation of the dualistic element, the scriptures would be falsified, and the Lord Himself would be guilty of an untruth. None of these three is considered either desirable or wholesome by the noble- minded.

sanskrit_shloka:
ईश्वरो वस्तुतत्त्वज्ञो न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ।
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानीत्येवमेव व्यचीकॢपत् ॥ २३३ ॥
transliteration:
īśvaro vastutattvajño na cāhaṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ |
na ca matsthāni bhūtānītyevameva vyacīkḷpat || 233 ||
translation: The Lord, who knows the secret of all things has supported this view in the words: 'But I am not in them' … 'nor are the beings in Me'.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Lord, who knows the secret of all things has supported this view in the words: 'But I am not in them' … 'nor are the beings in Me'.

sanskrit_shloka:
यदि सत्यं भवेद्विश्वं सुषुप्तामुपलभ्यताम् ।
यन्नोपलभ्यते किंचिदतोऽसत्स्वप्नवन्मृषा ॥ २३४ ॥
transliteration:
yadi satyaṃ bhavedviśvaṃ suṣuptāmupalabhyatām |
yannopalabhyate kiṃcidato'satsvapnavanmṛṣā || 234 ||
translation: If the universe be true, let it then be perceived in the state of deep sleep also. As it is not at all perceived, it must be unreal and false, like dreams.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: If the universe be true, let it then be perceived in the state of deep sleep also. As it is not at all perceived, it must be unreal and false, like dreams.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतः पृथङ्नास्ति जगत्परात्मनः पृथक्प्रतीतिस्तु मृषा गुणादिवत् ।
आरोपितस्यास्ति किमर्थवत्ताद् धिष्ठानमाभाति तथा भ्रमेण ॥ २३५ ॥
transliteration:
ataḥ pṛthaṅnāsti jagatparātmanaḥ pṛthakpratītistu mṛṣā guṇādivat |
āropitasyāsti kimarthavattād dhiṣṭhānamābhāti tathā bhrameṇa || 235 ||
translation: Therefore the universe does not exist apart from the Supreme Self; and the perception of its separateness is false like the qualities (of blueness etc., in the sky). Has a superimposed attribute any meaning apart from its substratum ? It is the substratum which appears like that through delusion.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Therefore the universe does not exist apart from the Supreme Self; and the perception of its separateness is false like the qualities (of blueness etc., in the sky). Has a superimposed attribute any meaning apart from its substratum ? It is the substratum which appears like that through delusion.

sanskrit_shloka:
भ्रान्तस्य यद्यद्भ्रमतः प्रतीतं भ्रामैव तत्तद्रजतं हि शुक्तिः ।
इदंतया ब्रह्म सदैव रूप्यते त्वारोपितं ब्रह्मणि नाममात्रम् ॥ २३६ ॥
transliteration:
bhrāntasya yadyadbhramataḥ pratītaṃ bhrāmaiva tattadrajataṃ hi śuktiḥ |
idaṃtayā brahma sadaiva rūpyate tvāropitaṃ brahmaṇi nāmamātram || 236 ||
translation: Whatever a deluded man perceives through mistake, is Brahman and Brahman alone: The silver is nothing but the mother-of-pearl. It is Brahman which is always considered as this universe, whereas that which is superimposed on the Brahman, viz. the universe, is merely a name.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Whatever a deluded man perceives through mistake, is Brahman and Brahman alone: The silver is nothing but the mother-of-pearl. It is Brahman which is always considered as this universe, whereas that which is superimposed on the Brahman, viz. the universe, is merely a name.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतः परं ब्रह्म सदद्वितीयं विशुद्धविज्ञानघनं निरञ्जनम् ।
प्राशान्तमाद्यन्तविहीनमक्रियं निरन्तरानन्दरसस्वरूपम् ॥ २३७ ॥
transliteration:
निरस्तमायाकृतसर्वभेदं नित्यं सुखं निष्कलमप्रमेयम् ।
अरूपमव्यक्तमनाख्यमव्ययं ज्योतिः स्वयं किंचिदिदं चकास्ति ॥ २३८ ॥
translation: 237-238. Hence whatever is manifested, viz. this universe, is the Supreme Brahman Itself, the Real, the One without a second, pure, the Essence of Knowledge, taintless, serene, devoid of beginning and end, beyond activity, the Essence of Bliss Absolute – transcending all the diversities created by Māyā or Nescience, eternal, ever beyond the reach of pain, indivisible, immeasurable, formless, undifferentiated, nameless, immutable, self-luminous.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: 237-238. Hence whatever is manifested, viz. this universe, is the Supreme Brahman Itself, the Real, the One without a second, pure, the Essence of Knowledge, taintless, serene, devoid of beginning and end, beyond activity, the Essence of Bliss Absolute – transcending all the diversities created by Māyā or Nescience, eternal, ever beyond the reach of pain, indivisible, immeasurable, formless, undifferentiated, nameless, immutable, self-luminous.

sanskrit_shloka:
ज्ञातृज्ञेयज्ञानशून्यमनन्तं निर्विकल्पकम् ।
केवलाखण्डचिन्मात्रं परं तत्त्वं विदुर्बुधाः ॥ २३९ ॥
transliteration:
jñātṛjñeyajñānaśūnyamanantaṃ nirvikalpakam |
kevalākhaṇḍacinmātraṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ vidurbudhāḥ || 239 ||
translation: Sages realise the Supreme Truth, Brahman, in which there is no differentiation of knower, knowledge and known, which is infinite, transcendent, and the Essence of Knowledge Absolute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Sages realise the Supreme Truth, Brahman, in which there is no differentiation of knower, knowledge and known, which is infinite, transcendent, and the Essence of Knowledge Absolute.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहेयमनुपादेयं मनोवाचामगोचरम् ।
अप्रमेयमनाद्यन्तं ब्रह्म पूर्णमहं महः ॥ २४0 ॥
transliteration:
aheyamanupādeyaṃ manovācāmagocaram |
aprameyamanādyantaṃ brahma pūrṇamahaṃ mahaḥ || 240 ||
translation: Which can be neither thrown away nor taken up, which is beyond the reach of mind and speech, immeasurable, without beginning and end, the Whole, one’s very Self, and of surpassing glory.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Which can be neither thrown away nor taken up, which is beyond the reach of mind and speech, immeasurable, without beginning and end, the Whole, one’s very Self, and of surpassing glory.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहेयमनुपादेयं मनोवाचामगोचरम् ।
अप्रमेयमनाद्यन्तं ब्रह्म पूर्णमहं महः ॥ २४0 ॥
transliteration:
aheyamanupādeyaṃ manovācāmagocaram |
aprameyamanādyantaṃ brahma pūrṇamahaṃ mahaḥ || 240 ||
translation: Which can be neither thrown away nor taken up, which is beyond the reach of mind and speech, immeasurable, without beginning and end, the Whole, one’s very Self, and of surpassing glory.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Which can be neither thrown away nor taken up, which is beyond the reach of mind and speech, immeasurable, without beginning and end, the Whole, one’s very Self, and of surpassing glory.

sanskrit_shloka:
तत्त्वंपदाभ्यामभिधीयमानयोः ब्रह्मात्मनोः शोधितयोर्यदीत्थम् ।
श्रुत्या तयोस्तत्त्वमसीति सम्यग् एकत्वमेव प्रतिपाद्यते मुहुः ॥ २४१
transliteration:
अइक्यं तयोर्लक्षितयोर्न वाच्ययोः निगद्यतेऽन्योन्यविरुद्धधर्मिणोः ।
खद्योतभान्वोरिव राजभृत्ययोः कूपाम्बुराश्योः परमाणुमेर्वोः ॥ २४२ ॥
translation: 241-242. If thus the Śruti, in the dictum 'Thou art That' (Tat-Tvam-Asi), repeatedly establishes the absolute identity of Brahman (or Ishwara) and Jīva, denoted by the terms That (Tat) and thou (Tvam) respectively, divesting these terms of their relative associations, then it is the identity of their implied, not literal, meanings which is sought to be inculcated; for they are of contradictory attributes to each other – like the sun and a glow-worm, the king and a servant, the ocean and a well, or Mount Meru and an atom.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: 241-242. If thus the Śruti, in the dictum 'Thou art That' (Tat-Tvam-Asi), repeatedly establishes the absolute identity of Brahman (or Ishwara) and Jīva, denoted by the terms That (Tat) and thou (Tvam) respectively, divesting these terms of their relative associations, then it is the identity of their implied, not literal, meanings which is sought to be inculcated; for they are of contradictory attributes to each other – like the sun and a glow-worm, the king and a servant, the ocean and a well, or Mount Meru and an atom.

sanskrit_shloka:
तयोर्विरोधोऽयमुपाधिकल्पितो न वास्तवः कश्चिदुपाधिरेषः ।
ईशस्य माया महदादिकारणं जीवस्य कार्यं शृणु पञ्चकोशम् ॥ २४३ ॥
transliteration:
tayorvirodho'yamupādhikalpito na vāstavaḥ kaścidupādhireṣaḥ |
īśasya māyā mahadādikāraṇaṃ jīvasya kāryaṃ śṛṇu pañcakośam || 243 ||
translation: This contradiction between them is created by superimposition, and is not something real. This superimposition, in the case of Ishwara (the Lord), is Māyā or Nescience, which is the cause of Mahat and the rest, and in the case of the Jiva (the individual soul), listen – the five sheaths, which are the effects of Māyā, stand for it.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This contradiction between them is created by superimposition, and is not something real. This superimposition, in the case of Ishwara (the Lord), is Māyā or Nescience, which is the cause of Mahat and the rest, and in the case of the Jiva (the individual soul), listen – the five sheaths, which are the effects of Māyā, stand for it.

sanskrit_shloka:
एतावुपाधी परजीवयोस्तयोः सम्यङ्निरासे न परो न जीवः ।
राज्यं नरेन्द्रस्य भटस्य खेटक् तयोरपोहे न भटो न राजा ॥ २४४ ॥
transliteration:
etāvupādhī parajīvayostayoḥ samyaṅnirāse na paro na jīvaḥ |
rājyaṃ narendrasya bhaṭasya kheṭak tayorapohe na bhaṭo na rājā || 244 ||
translation: These two are the superimpositions of Ishwara and the Jiva respectively, and when these are perfectly eliminated, there is neither Ishwara nor Jiva. A kingdom is the symbol of a king, and a shield of the soldier, and when these are taken away, there is neither king nor soldier.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: These two are the superimpositions of Ishwara and the Jiva respectively, and when these are perfectly eliminated, there is neither Ishwara nor Jiva. A kingdom is the symbol of a king, and a shield of the soldier, and when these are taken away, there is neither king nor soldier.

sanskrit_shloka:
अथात आदेश इति श्रुतिः स्वयं निषेधति ब्रह्मणि कल्पितं द्वयम् ।
श्रुतिप्रमाणानुगृहीतबोधात् तयोर्निरासः करणीय एव ॥ २४५ ॥
transliteration:
athāta ādeśa iti śrutiḥ svayaṃ niṣedhati brahmaṇi kalpitaṃ dvayam |
śrutipramāṇānugṛhītabodhāt tayornirāsaḥ karaṇīya eva || 245 ||
translation: The Vedas themselves in the words 'now then is the injunction' etc., repudiate the duality imagined in Brahman. One must needs eliminate those two superimpositions by means of realisation supported by the authority of the Vedas.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Vedas themselves in the words 'now then is the injunction' etc., repudiate the duality imagined in Brahman. One must needs eliminate those two superimpositions by means of realisation supported by the authority of the Vedas.

sanskrit_shloka:
नेदं नेदं कल्पितत्वान्न सत्यं रज्जुदृष्टव्यालवत्स्वप्नवच्च ।
इत्थं दृश्यं साधुयुक्त्या व्यपोह्य ज्ञेयः पश्चादेकभावस्तयोर्यः ॥ २४६ ॥
transliteration:
nedaṃ nedaṃ kalpitatvānna satyaṃ rajjudṛṣṭavyālavatsvapnavacca |
itthaṃ dṛśyaṃ sādhuyuktyā vyapohya jñeyaḥ paścādekabhāvastayoryaḥ || 246 ||
translation: Neither this gross nor this subtle universe (is the Ātman). Being imagined, they are not real – like the snake seen in the rope, and like dreams. Perfectly eliminating the objective world in this way by means of reasoning, one should next realise the oneness that underlies Ishwara and the Jiva.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Neither this gross nor this subtle universe (is the Ātman). Being imagined, they are not real – like the snake seen in the rope, and like dreams. Perfectly eliminating the objective world in this way by means of reasoning, one should next realise the oneness that underlies Ishwara and the Jiva.

sanskrit_shloka:
ततस्तु तौ लक्षणया सुलक्ष्यौ तयोरखण्डैकरसत्वसिद्धये ।
नालं जहत्या न तथाजहत्या किन्तूभयार्थात्मिकयैव भाव्यम् ॥ २४७ ॥
transliteration:
tatastu tau lakṣaṇayā sulakṣyau tayorakhaṇḍaikarasatvasiddhaye |
nālaṃ jahatyā na tathājahatyā kintūbhayārthātmikayaiva bhāvyam || 247 ||
translation: Hence those two terms (Ishwara and Jīva) must be carefully considered through their implied meanings, so that their absolute identity may be established. Neither the method of total rejection nor that of complete retention will do. One must reason out through the process which combines the two.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Hence those two terms (Ishwara and Jīva) must be carefully considered through their implied meanings, so that their absolute identity may be established. Neither the method of total rejection nor that of complete retention will do. One must reason out through the process which combines the two.

sanskrit_shloka:
स देवदत्तोऽयमितीह चैकता विरुद्धधर्मांशमपास्य कथ्यते ।
यथा तथा तत्त्वमसीतिवाक्ये विरुद्धधर्मानुभयत्र हित्वा ॥ २४८ ॥
transliteration:
संलक्ष्य चिन्मात्रतया सदात्मनोः अखण्डभावः परिचीयते बुधैः ।
एवं महावाक्यशतेन कथ्यते ब्रह्मात्मनोरैक्यमखण्डभावः ॥ २४९ ॥
translation: 248-249. Just as in the sentence, 'This is that Devadatta', the identity is spoken of, eliminating the contradictory portions, so in the sentence 'Thou art That', the wise man must give up the contradictory elements on both sides and recognise the identity of Ishwara and Jīva, noticing carefully the essence of both, which is Chit, Knowledge Absolute. Thus hundreds of scriptural texts inculcate the oneness and identity of Brahman and Jīva.

translation: sa devadatto'yamitīha caikatā viruddhadharmāṃśamapāsya kathyate | yathā tathā tattvamasītivākye viruddhadharmānubhayatra hitvā || 248 ||

sanskrit_shloka:
एकमेव सदनेककारणं कारणान्तरनिरास्यकारणम् ।
कार्यकारणविलक्षणं स्वयं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २६0 ॥
transliteration:
ekameva sadanekakāraṇaṃ kāraṇāntaranirāsyakāraṇam |
kāryakāraṇavilakṣaṇaṃ svayaṃ brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 260 ||
translation: That which, though One only, is the cause of the many; which refutes all other causes, but is Itself without cause; distinct from Māyā and its effect, the universe; and independent – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
अस्थूलमित्येतदसन्निरस्य सिद्धं स्वतो व्योमवदप्रतर्क्यम् ।
अतो मृषामात्रमिदं प्रतीतं जहीहि यत्स्वात्मतया गृहीतम् ब्रह्माहमित्येव विशुद्धबुद्ध्या विद्धि स्वमात्मानमखण्डबोधम् ॥ २५0 ॥
transliteration:
asthūlamityetadasannirasya siddhaṃ svato vyomavadapratarkyam |
ato mṛṣāmātramidaṃ pratītaṃ jahīhi yatsvātmatayā gṛhītam brahmāhamityeva viśuddhabuddhyā viddhi svamātmānamakhaṇḍabodham || 250 ||
translation: Eliminating the not-Self, in the light of such passages as 'It is not gross' etc., (one realises the Ātman), which is self-established, unattached like the sky, and beyond the range of thought. Therefore dismiss this mere phantom of a body which thou perceivest and hast accepted as thy own self. By means of the purified understanding that thou art Brahman, realise thy own self, the Knowledge Absolute.
